clue.text: Art embodying very personal features?

parts.note: a picture whose subject is the painter's own face, so the features shown are as personal as they get

explanation.surface: A remark about deeply intimate artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's likeness of themself shows their own facial features, the most personal art there is.

clue.text: Lines making cuttings in SE slopes

parts.note: taken as written, the compass abbreviation for south-east
cants are slopes or tilts

explanation.surface: Railway or road cuttings being dug into slopes in the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuttings' suggests excavations, but in geometry a secant is a line that cuts a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, straight lines that intersect a curve at two points are named for cutting it.

clue.text: Articles HM's placed in glass frames

indicators.note: something placed in a frame sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: leads are the strips of lead holding the panes in a leaded window
HM is Her Majesty, ER (Elizabeth Regina); the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Items about the monarch being displayed in glass cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'HM's placed in' as 'HM is placed in'. Leaders are newspaper editorials, also called leading articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders are a newspaper's editorial pieces, its leading articles.

clue.text: Bottled-up — concealing unorthodox creed, for example

indicators.note: a word that conceals something holds it hidden inside itself

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means bottled-up

indicators.note: an unorthodox version departs from the standard form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone repressed hides an unconventional belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled-up' looks like the definition, but it supplies the container; the definition is 'example' at the far end, with 'for' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A precedent is an earlier case serving as a model or instance to follow.

clue.text: Controlled game, playing first

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
in card games, the player who plays first has led

explanation.surface: A game carefully supervised with one side starting.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) is a sport popular in Britain; to lead in cards is to play the first card of a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled is a synonym of governed or held in check.

clue.text: Quickly moved chess piece, having distinctive position

parts.note: ran means moved quickly
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A chess piece shifted swiftly to a strong square.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking officer holds a senior, marked status above others.

clue.text: CIA to be redeployed in craft with runners

indicators.note: redeployed agents are moved around into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: American intelligence agents being reassigned to a vessel on runners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is part of the fodder and of the indicator phrase only in surface; the anagram uses CIA, TO and BE.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceboat is a sailing vessel mounted on skate-like blades for travelling over ice.

clue.text: Fruit (pound) to be used in second course, we're told

indicators.note: something used in another item goes inside it, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
L is the abbreviation for pound (from libra)

indicators.note: signals that the word for course is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a current is a course or flow, as of a river

explanation.surface: A fruit costing a pound served in the second course of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be used in' puts L inside BACK for BLACK; 'we're told' turns CURRENT into the fruit's spelling. The bracketed 'pound' looks like a price.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackcurrant is a small dark berry grown on a garden bush.

clue.text: Barge tolls become fixed with time

parts.note: to lock is to become fixed or jammed in place
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Canal charges set rigidly over a period.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockage is the fee charged for passing a vessel through a canal lock.

clue.text: Origin of flax spinning in Leeds

indicators.note: spinning turns things round, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Flax being spun in the Yorkshire city of Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a northern English city long known for textiles, so 'spinning' fits the surface as well as signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed is the seed of the flax plant, from which the crop is grown.

clue.text: Study letter about huntsman's third meet

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, as something about a centre surrounds it

parts.note: vee is the spelt-out name of the letter V

indicators.note: picks the third letter of the word huntsman

explanation.surface: Studying a letter about the huntsman at a hunt meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to assemble or come together for a gathering.

clue.text: Fiends, mean fellows outwardly

indicators.note: the word for fellows sits on the outside, wrapping the other piece

parts.note: dons are university fellows
to aim is to mean or intend

explanation.surface: Calling some stingy university fellows devils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like an adjective (stingy) but it is a verb, AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Daimons are spirits or demons in Greek mythology, a variant of demons.

clue.text: Patients' specimens

definitions.meaning: a doctor's patients are spoken of as ...

explanation.definitionFit: Doctors call the people they treat their cases, and a case is also an instance or example of something.

clue.text: Measure to cheer up and edify

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure
to lighten is to cheer up or relieve gloom

explanation.surface: A step taken to raise spirits and improve someone's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten is to instruct or improve someone morally and mentally.

clue.text: Keen about trendy English trait

indicators.note: the word for keen goes round the other letters

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to lament
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: An eager person mentions a fashionable English quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective (eager) but is the verb to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineament is a distinctive feature or characteristic, especially of the face.

clue.text: Dashed off again?

parts.note: something written quickly a second time; dashed off means quickly penned

explanation.definitionFit: Writing a piece out a second time, perhaps in haste, means it has been redone in words.

clue.text: Dictionary needed for English dramatist

definitions.meaning: Noah ... compiled the best-known American dictionary
John ... wrote the Jacobean tragedy The Duchess of Malfi

explanation.definitionFit: Merriam-Webster is a standard American dictionary, and John Webster was a Jacobean playwright.

clue.text: One motorway, after Bury, is temporary?

indicators.note: the pieces before it come after the word for bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a motorway after the town of Bury is only provisional.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, which tempts the solver to read it as a place; here it is the verb. The definition with 'is' reads as 'what is temporary', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes an arrangement lasting only for the meantime, provisional.

clue.text: Animal, no royal emblem

indicators.note: says a letter is absent from the animal's name

parts.note: the badger is an animal
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: An animal that is not a royal symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is a distinguishing sign or symbol worn to show allegiance.

clue.text: Depth's short in little mind

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a bit is a little

indicators.note: the word for depth is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: an abyss is an immense depth; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A remark about someone of limited intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last S of ABYSS, leaving ABYS, which goes into BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to look after children, as in minding them while the parents are out.

clue.text: Rested for day, then rose

parts.note: welled means rose up, as water from a spring

explanation.surface: Someone took a break for a day, then got up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower or 'got up', but it is water welling.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell on or upon something is to linger or remain, an older sense of staying put.

clue.text: Trade Union, to revolutionary, was mentor

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A trade union official, turned radical, acted as an adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tutored someone is to have coached and guided them.

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests St Paul's letters to the Corinthians; the Corinthians were Greeks, so a letter of their alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth character of the Greek alphabet used in Corinth.
